title: NFL joint simulation draw archive
why_this_exists: MLB stored nine percentiles. That cannot support exact CRPS, log score, or tail calibration, and it is why board_config's graded_prediction_means requirement is unmet for the MLB development set.

NFL correlation is mechanically stronger and is checkable rather than argued: passer_player_id, receiver_player_id and td_player_id sit on the SAME play row, so one draw credits two players by construction.

Independent marginal draws would reproduce every marginal correctly and get the joint wrong. Since correlation is the entire product for stacking and any multi-player question, marginals are not a cheaper version of the right answer.
Sizing is not a reason to skip it: 540 integers per sim-game over 272 games is ~2.94 GB/season at 10,000 sims, about one fifth of the MLB equivalent.

execution_identity_fingerprint.description: Binds the archive to the identity that produced it, INCLUDING the sha256 of every consumed input partition.

seed.description: Required and nullable. null means 'deterministic, no RNG', which is a claim the determinism test checks; omitting the field entirely is not permitted.

cross_game_dependence.description: REQUIRED. Whether sim_index i in this archive is aligned with sim_index i in another game's archive. Cross-game sim_index alignment is valid ONLY while games are independent; treating unaligned archives as aligned silently fabricates correlation across games, which is the trap that MLB's experience does not cover.

basis.description: UNDECLARED is permitted in the schema so it can be recorded honestly, and is refused by the consumer. It is not a default.

draws.description: One row per simulation. Empty is a FAIL, never an empty success.
